text: The legal doctrine of qualified immunity in civil rights litigation presents a persistent barrier to constitutional accountability. By shielding government officials from liability unless they violate clearly established statutory or constitutional rights, the doctrine creates a self-reinforcing procedural impediment. Lower courts frequently dismiss complaints on the second prong without determining whether the underlying conduct was constitutional, thereby freezing the evolution of substantive constitutional standards. Reforming this doctrine is essential to restoring public confidence in institutional remedies.
